PullRequest.Title: agentHost: preserve read-only session configuration values
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Fixes a regression introduced by #339034: client-side schema filtering dropped settings-derived worktree configuration because the host marks these properties `readOnly`. In particular, `git.worktreeSymlinkFolders` stopped reaching the host, so folders such as `node_modules` were no longer symlinked into new worktrees.

- Ignore `readOnly` in session config validation/filtering and in the pre-send settings refresh. Pickers still honor `readOnly` for UI editability; advertised-key, enum, and session-mutability checks remain unchanged.
- Restore forwarding of branch prefixes, included files, symlink folders, branch tracking, and the create-new-branch option.
- Match the provider test schema to the real host and cover creation, resolution, folder-settings refresh/clearing, programmatic worktree configuration, and read-only mutable values such as shell initialization scripts.
- Update workbench tests to expect read-only values to remain in resolution and completion payloads.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create a new Agent Host session with settings-derived worktree configuration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Schema discovery must complete before the draft config is ready; eager createSession then uses the resolved values. The diff changes which values survive filtering but does not add a new API stage.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the provider schema/config, with an optional second resolve when seeded values differ from discovered values.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One discovery request and at most one follow-up request per draft resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same discovery/follow-up algorithm existed, but readOnly settings carriers and host-reported values were removed from payloads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Discovery is on draft configuration readiness; a follow-up is required before the resolved config is committed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create the backend session with the resolved config.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One eager create request per draft, with existing fallback behavior on failure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same create request occurred with readOnly properties omitted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs eagerly before first send and is awaited there; the diff only increases the config payload by advertised read-only values.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number and size of advertised config values, principally a branch prefix and user-configured include/symlink pattern arrays; no collection-to-request fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Configuration discovery and any follow-up resolution are awaited serially per draft. Eager create is one task per NewSession; the diff adds no parallel fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The resolved schema and values are retained on NewSession. Discovery is cold per new draft; subsequent reads use the cached result. No changed cache key or negative-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that payloads are richer while request cardinality and serialization points are unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider-specific readOnly values can vary, but repository-defined values are small and bounded in normal use; exact IPC serialization cost is not measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the extra serialization is proportional to the existing config payload and restores settings explicitly configured for session creation without adding boundary calls or unbounded retained state.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send the first prompt for a worktree-isolated session after folder settings load
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The provider re-reads three settings-derived values before sending. On the host, first-send worktree materialization performs git checkout and then configured symlink/copy work before the turn can start.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send updated session config and the first chat request through the existing session path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one settings refresh over three fixed keys immediately before the first send; only changed values are written.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The refresh existed, but skipped readOnly worktree carrier properties.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The refresh is synchronous in-memory work; subsequent existing config/send dispatches carry the corrected values.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run git repository discovery, optional fetch, and git worktree add.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One materialization per worktree session; branch/worktree creation is sequenced per repository.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Worktree checkout already occurred for worktree isolation; the changed values affect branch naming/tracking but do not add another checkout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before the first turn starts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve configured patterns, create symlinks, and copy matched ignored files into the new worktree.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One pass per new worktree; work scales with configured patterns and effective matched files/folders, with 15 concurrent operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: In the immediate base revision these settings-derived readOnly values were filtered, so their configured symlink/copy operations were skipped.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs after checkout and before first-turn progress can complete.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective matched ignored files and folders after user-configured patterns; one worktree per session and no repeated execution after materialization.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Worktree creation is sequenced per repository. Symlink and include-file operations use limiters of 15, and materialization is cached by session ID so re-entry reuses the worktree.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The materialized worktree map is the warm cache and avoids repeated creation/copy work for the session. Empty settings clear prior carriers; there is no negative-cache loop introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the filesystem/subprocess path, its first-send placement, limiter, and one-time lifecycle.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Copy duration depends on user-selected files and repository size, but this is explicitly requested worktree behavior rather than accidental fan-out.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the newly reachable file operations are the intended semantics of git.worktreeIncludeFiles and git.worktreeSymlinkFolders, are user-configured, bounded to one materialization, and concurrency-limited.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open and filter a dynamic session-config picker, including a remote Agent Host
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening a dynamic picker awaits one completions request; non-branch filtering waits for a 200 ms Delayer and then awaits another request. Branch items are loaded once for the picker and filtered locally.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize current config and request dynamic values from the Agent Host/provider; remote connections may carry this over a network-backed protocol.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request on picker open plus one per coalesced non-branch query; branch filtering uses the already loaded list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same completion requests occurred, but readOnly values such as locked reports or shellInitScripts were omitted from each config payload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each request gates updated picker options.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of coalesced filter queries and byte size of retained readOnly config. The built-in shell initializer produces one script described as a few hundred bytes, has a 64 KiB validation cap, and is not published in remote-development windows.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The 200 ms Delayer coalesces rapid filter input. No new requests are launched by retaining readOnly values, and the branch path avoids per-keystroke remote calls.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Branch results are cached for a NewSession and picker-local branch results are reused. Generic dynamic provider queries are not cached but are coalesced by the 200 ms Delayer; the diff changes neither behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that payload size increases and request count does not; low confidence that the bounded extra bytes have user-visible cost.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Third-party providers could advertise larger readOnly values, but no realistic repository path establishes enough repeated bytes to create material latency or throughput loss.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: this is a small payload increase on existing coalesced requests, with no boundary fan-out or realistic evidence of user-visible serialization/network impact.

Scenarios.Scenario: Edit or replace running session configuration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A user edit dispatches the changed property and, except for sandbox-only changes, starts one resolveSessionConfig request whose latest sequence wins. Replace dispatches one full replacement and starts one resolve.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Re-resolve running config after an edit, now carrying advertised readOnly values in addition to mutable values.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One resolve per qualifying user config edit; replacement likewise triggers one existing resolve.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same resolve request was issued with readOnly values filtered out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The optimistic local update proceeds before resolution; this request is off the immediate UI critical path, though it updates authoritative config when complete.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: User config-edit frequency and config payload size; no per-property request loop is added.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Calls are not globally serialized, but stale responses are discarded by a per-session sequence. The diff does not increase the number of edits, dispatches, or resolves.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Current running config is retained per session and replaced by the latest successful sequence. No cache invalidation, miss retry, or retention lifecycle changes are introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in unchanged request cardinality and asynchronous optimistic behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider-defined readOnly payload sizes vary, but edits are user-driven and repository-defined values are small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: richer payloads preserve host-owned state but do not add synchronous UI work, requests, or unbounded memory.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all seven changed files and traced session creation, first-send worktree materialization, dynamic picker completion, and running-config update paths. The diff restores read-only carrier values and modestly enlarges existing config payloads; it adds no repeated boundary calls, unbounded retention, eager heavyweight allocation, or missing coalescing. The only newly reachable filesystem work is explicit, one-time, concurrency-limited behavior requested by worktree settings. No performance finding or qualifying regression-fix record was supported.
